title: Events contract compatibility and validator tooling
creator: Daniel Morales
description: Problem: As we expand SDKs/CLI surface area and add multiple ingestion endpoints (hosted API, dedicated edge, private), we are seeing intermittent schema incompatibilities causing downstream pipeline rejections, silent field drops, and incorrect cost attribution. Goal: Define a clear versioning and backward/forward compatibility contract for events sent from SDK/CLI/API + build validator tooling (local CLI check + CI gate + runtime inbound validator) to detect and remediate schema drift before it impacts ingestion. Deliverables: 1) Events contract spec and compatibility rules (semver-like for analytics fields) 2) A lightweight portable validator library (Go/TS) with pluggable rules and auto-migrations 3) CI/PR check for SDK/CLI changes plus a pre-commit hook template 4) Runtime ingestion validator with a fast reject/transform path + metrics/alerting 5) Migration & rollout playbook for field deprecations and required producers
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc published with explicit backward/forward compatibility matrix and upgrade rules
Validator library published in monorepo with Go and TypeScript bindings and README
SDK and CLI include the validator in CI; PRs adding event fields fail fast on schema violations
Ingress service runs validator at edge; violations emit schema_violation_count and sample payload to safe-sink
Canary migration plan documented and tested (small percentage traffic + automatic rollback on >0.5% rejection rate)
comments: 2025-02-18 Daniel Morales: Created ticket after repeated ingestion rejections from SDK v0.9.3 — initial spike correlated with new trace_id field being sent as integer instead of string.
2025-02-22 Priya Singh: Drafted compatibility rules in Confluence (link above). Proposing rule: additive fields are allowed if optional and validated by validator with a default null/backfill policy.
2025-02-25 Engineering sync: Decided runtime validator will operate in two modes: strict (reject) and permissive (transform & warn). Default to permissive during rollout window.
2025-02-28 Román Alvarez (SDK): Added validator hook to TypeScript SDK CI; found 3 field naming inconsistencies across SDKs. Patch PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/112

2025-03-03 SRE: Added observability requirements. Metrics to instrument: schema_violation_count, sdk_version_mismatch, transformed_event_count, validation_latency_ms. Dashboards draft available in Console -> Observability -> Schema
2025-03-04 Priya Singh: MVP validator library v0.1 published to monorepo. Next: add Go binding and CLI binary, prepare PR gate integration. Assigned follow-ups for backfill tasks.
runbook: Pre-deploy: run local validator against fixtures (tools/validators/fixtures). CI: include validator in PR checks for SDKs and CLI. Canary: enable strict mode for 2% of traffic for 48h, monitor schema_violation_count and transformed_event_count. Rollback: toggle permissive mode and revert SDK change if >0.5% strict rejections for 6h. Post-mortem: capture sample violations, owners, and deploy follow-up patch within 3 days.
notes: Validator will expose an opt-in auto-migrate function for safe renames (rename map in spec). For high-volume fields we will prefer server-side transform rather than client changes to avoid churn. Consider embedding schema-version header (X-Events-Schema: 2025-01) to help routing to specialized parsers.
implementation_details: Library API: Validate(payload, schemaVersion) -> {status, diagnostics, migrationHints}. CLI binary 'rw-schema-check' will accept --fixtures and --mode (strict|permissive). Ingress: apply validator in pre-ingest filter with bounded CPU (use small wasm shim for TypeScript SDKs) and send samples of failures to safe-sink S3 with kms encryption. CI: add GH Action that runs validator against generated event examples from SDK change set.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false positives break PR velocity. Mitigation: start permissive with warnings and add diagnostic links in CI failure messages. Risk: performance impact on ingestion path. Mitigation: run lightweight validation checks (shape & typed-headers) and offload heavy schema transforms to background worker. Risk: older SDKs not updated. Mitigation: embed schema-version header and route to compatibility layer supporting legacy shapes.
next_steps: 1) Finalize spec and publish by 2025-03-07. 2) Complete Go binding and CLI by 2025-03-12. 3) Integrate CI gate for SDK repo and roll to permissive runtime validator for 7 days. 4) Schedule canary strict mode and measure impact. 5) Coordinate communication to SDK consumers and update migration guide.
audit_trail: Linked PRs and Confluence pages archived. All CI run logs will be kept for 90 days and linked in final post-mortem.
